title: Nissen Fundoplication, Barrett Oesophagus, and Antireflux Surgery

steps.tx: The gold standard surgical therapy for severe, refractory gastroesophageal reflux disease is the **laparoscopic Nissen fundoplication**. This procedure mobilizes the gastric fundus and wraps it 360 degrees circumferentially around the lower intra-abdominal esophagus. Indications include persistent reflux symptoms despite optimal medical therapy, intolerance to lifetime proton pump inhibitor medication, large hiatal hernias, and severe extra-esophageal manifestations such as aspiration asthma and chronic laryngitis.
steps.say: Laparoscopic Nissen fundoplication is the benchmark anti-reflux operation, wrapping the gastric fundus 360 degrees around the lower esophagus to restore sphincter competence and stop acid reflux.

vis.caption: Anti-reflux surgery: restoring the lower esophageal sphincter high-pressure zone via fundic wrapping. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Before offering anti-reflux surgery, objective physiological testing is mandatory to confirm abnormal acid exposure and evaluate esophageal motility. Upper endoscopy assesses for mucosal erosions and hiatal hernia. Quantitative **24-hour ambulatory pH monitoring** is the gold standard for verifying pathological acid reflux, documented by a total acid exposure time greater than six percent or an elevated composite DeMeester score exceeding fourteen point seven.
steps.say: Preoperative evaluation requires 24-hour ambulatory pH monitoring to prove pathological acid reflux, defined by an elevated DeMeester score above fourteen point seven or excessive acid exposure.

steps.tx: Preoperative high-resolution manometry is essential to exclude underlying esophageal motor disorders like achalasia or severe ineffective esophageal motility. A patient with poor esophageal peristaltic reserve who receives a tight 360-degree wrap will suffer severe, intractable postoperative dysphagia. If esophageal motility is significantly impaired, the surgeon avoids a complete Nissen wrap and selects a partial fundoplication instead, such as a **posterior Toupet 270-degree wrap**.
steps.say: High-resolution manometry ensures the esophagus has sufficient peristaltic strength to push food through the wrap. Patients with poor motility receive a partial Toupet wrap instead.

steps.tx: The operative technique of a floppy Nissen fundoplication follows precise principles to prevent postoperative complications. The surgeon divides the short gastric vessels to fully mobilize the fundus, ensuring a tension-free wrap. A large fifty to sixty French bougie is placed intraluminally across the gastroesophageal junction during suturing. Constructing a short wrap measuring only **one and a half to two centimetres** around the calibrated bougie prevents the distressing complications of gas-bloat and dysphagia.
steps.say: A floppy Nissen wrap requires dividing the short gastric vessels, sizing the wrap over a large bougie, and keeping the wrap short, between one and a half and two centimeters in length.

steps.tx: A common complication of complete 360-degree fundoplication is **gas-bloat syndrome**. Because the tight wrap acts as a one-way valve, it prevents the patient from venting swallowed intragastric air through belching or vomiting. Patients experience severe postprandial fullness, epigastric distension, and increased flatus. Careful patient counseling regarding eating habits, avoiding carbonated beverages, and meticulous intraoperative floppy wrap construction substantially mitigate this adverse effect.
steps.say: Gas-bloat syndrome develops when a tight wrap prevents belching, trapping swallowed air in the stomach. Constructing a floppy wrap and avoiding carbonated drinks minimizes this problem.

steps.tx: Chronic acid and bile reflux over many years drives the development of **Barrett oesophagus**, a premier premalignant condition. Pathologically, it is defined by the metaplastic replacement of normal stratified squamous epithelium of the distal esophagus by specialized intestinal-type columnar epithelium containing mucin-secreting goblet cells. This metaplastic transformation represents a physiological adaptation to chronic acidic exposure, but carries an increased risk of progression to esophageal adenocarcinoma.
steps.say: Barrett esophagus develops when chronic acid reflux causes the normal squamous lining of the distal esophagus to be replaced by intestinal-type columnar epithelium with goblet cells.

vis.alt: Histopathological and endoscopic diagram showing the transition from normal squamous mucosa to Barrett columnar metaplasia.
vis.caption: Barrett oesophagus: metaplastic transformation from squamous epithelium to mucinous columnar cells. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Endoscopic inspection of Barrett esophagus utilizes the standardized **Prague C and M criteria**. The circumferential extent (C) measures the continuous circular length of columnar mucosa above the gastroesophageal junction, while the maximal extent (M) records the highest reaching columnar tongue. Four-quadrant jumbo biopsies are obtained every one to two centimetres following the Seattle protocol to detect early dysplasia. Chromoendoscopy or narrow-band imaging highlights mucosal architectural irregularities to guide targeted biopsies.
steps.say: Endoscopy grades Barrett esophagus using the Prague criteria, measuring circumferential and maximal length. Four-quadrant biopsies taken every two centimeters screen for dysplasia.

steps.tx: The management of Barrett esophagus depends on the histological degree of dysplasia. Non-dysplastic Barrett esophagus is managed with acid suppression and endoscopic surveillance every three to five years. When confirmed low-grade or high-grade dysplasia is identified, endoscopic eradication therapy is recommended. Focal nodular lesions are excised via **endoscopic mucosal resection** for precise pathological staging, followed by circumferential radiofrequency ablation of the remaining flat Barrett segment.
steps.say: Non-dysplastic Barrett esophagus requires surveillance every three to five years. Dysplastic Barrett is treated with endoscopic mucosal resection of raised nodules and radiofrequency ablation of flat mucosa.

rows: Surveillance every 6 to 12 months if untreated
